findings.reason: The diff deletes the `node.tag !== defaultScalarTag.tagName` early return, so applyForceQuotesOption now quotes any plain non-key scalar. presenter.ts:417 prints the tag for any non-plain scalar whose tag isn't the default string tag, and this goes against the documented contract at presenter.ts:99 ('Quotes all non-key strings').
findings.claim: Removing the default-scalar-tag guard makes forceQuotes quote non-string scalars (ints, floats, booleans, null), which then print with explicit tags such as `!!int '1'`.
findings.evidence: The diff deletes `if (layout.node.tag !== layout.presenterOptions.schema.defaultScalarTag.tagName) return` and rewrites the comment to 'applies only to plain values'. src/ast/presenter.ts:99 still documents the option as 'Quotes all non-key strings', and CHANGELOG.md:134 says 'force quoting non-key strings'. For a quoted non-str node, src/ast/presenter.ts:417 `(layout.style !== SCALAR_STYLE.PLAIN && node.tag !== state.defaultScalarTagName)` makes the presenter print an explicit tag, so every number, boolean and null gets a verbose `!!int`/`!!bool`/`!!null` tag.

findings.reason: dump-options.test.mjs:93-103 and dump-scalar-styles.test.mjs:107 only dump string values with forceQuotes, and the diff adds no test. The gap is real. I lowered severity to low because it is a missing test for the C1/X1 defect, not a separate defect.
findings.claim: forceQuotes tests only cover string values, so the regression for non-string scalars isn't caught.
findings.evidence: The test 'forceQuotes — quotes non-key strings using quoteStyle' only asserts on `{ hello: 'world' }`. No test dumps a number, boolean or null with `forceQuotes: true`, and the diff adds no test of its own.
